newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African bonds end sharply firmer, helped by U.S..
newsitem.headline: S.African bonds end sharply firmer, helped by U.S..

text.p: 1408 GMT - Bonds end sharply firmer on good offshore interest and local short-covering. Rand little changed after range-bound day.

* Key R150 last at 14.70 pct from 14.86 pct on Friday. Dealers say market buoyed by good offshore interest on the day, linked to possible hedging of two new zero-coupon bonds, as well as local short-covering.

* Helped by lower U.S. T-bond yield, which plunges to last trade at 7.01 pct from 7.13 pct before better-than-expected first quarter employment cost index and March durable goods orders data released at 1230 GMT.

* R150 struggles to move below 14.70 pct level as selling emerges, possibly options-related ahead of Friday's close-out. Activity on the day generally quiet with some players away ahead of market holiday on Thursday. Seen holding 14.75 to 14.65 pct range on Wednesday.

* Rand last at 4.4415/4445 on dollar from 4.4510/4540 late on Friday. Dealers say trade on the day characterised by local importer demand and offshore dollar selling. Volumes thin. Rand expected to remain range-bound on Wednesday.
